real_qa.q: What is Bonds' internal marketing mantra to maintain brand consistency and create iconic campaigns?
real_qa.r: The internal mantra that all of the team lives by is 'do iconic shit.' It's the question that we ask of the creative, it's the question that we ask about agencies, and it's the way that we induct and train our teams on how we want to bring the brand to life—asking is it iconic, are we doing iconic shit, or could anyone do it?

real_qa.q: How did Bonds launch into the U.S. market with the Robert Irwin 'Made for Down Under' campaign?
real_qa.r: The campaign was designed to celebrate Bonds' launch into the U.S. market and featured Robert Irwin in his underwear, taking the simple idea that Australians are laid back in the face of danger, suggesting it's because they're all wearing comfy undies. It was executed as a one-take, one-shot ad that was unapologetically Aussie and cut through in America almost overnight, going viral and appearing on the news.

real_qa.q: How many Bonds products does the average Australian household own?
real_qa.r: Bonds has 12 items in every household on average in Australia. This ubiquity was central to the brand's U.S. launch proposition, and similar campaigns are based around this idea of Bonds being omnipresent.

real_qa.q: What is the size and structure of Bonds' marketing team?
real_qa.r: Bonds has a marketing team of 30 people split across Australia and Bangkok. The team spans core brand marketing, social media, content, visual merchandising, graphic design, and an in-house studio, providing wide-reaching expertise across many touchpoints.

real_qa.q: What key lesson did Bonds' head of marketing learn from expanding into the U.S. market?
real_qa.r: The biggest lesson was the importance of simplicity and trusting gut instinct to translate the brand. When taking Bonds to a brand new audience that had never heard of it before, the need to boil everything down to just a few core ingredients became a gift to creativity—simplicity in both strategy and craft, which also taught lessons about not overcomplicating marketing even in the home market.

real_qa.r: Ketek Azarian has been with Bonds for 12 years.
